---
title: Intro to Entities BP
category: General
nav_order: 1
tags:
    - guide
    - beginner
mentions:
    - SirLich
    - solvedDev
    - stirante
    - Joelant05
    - destruc7ion
    - MedicalJewel105
    - ChibiMango
    - SmokeyStack
    - ThomasOrs
description: Introduction to entities behavior pack.
---

Three main structures make up the base of a behavior-pack entity file. This document will explain what each of them means and how to use them.

Confusing component groups with components is a widespread source of errors. Pay attention closely to understand the difference.

## Components

Components are logical building blocks that make up Minecraft entities. All components are written by Mojang and provided to us for use. Components can do all sorts of things, like set the size of an entity or give it the ability to swim. The complete list of components can be found [here](https://bedrock.dev/docs/stable/Entities).

It is _impossible_ to create your own components. The entire list of components is hard-coded and provided by Microsoft.

When you want to add behavior to your entity, you add `components` into the `components` object of the `minecraft:entity` object. For example, if we want to give the entity the ability to climb, we can do so by adding this component: `"minecraft:can_climb": {}`.

All components are formatted like `"minecraft:<name>": { <setting> }`. Every component takes different kinds of settings.

Here is an example of a few components, inside an entity:

<CodeHeader path="BP/entities/example.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:entity" />

```json
"components": {
    "minecraft:type_family": {
        "family": [
            "player"
        ]
    },
    "minecraft:collision_box": {
        "width": 0.6,
        "height": 1.8
    },
    "minecraft:can_climb": {}
}
```

Notice how the `components` list _only_ contains components.

## Component Groups

Component groups are "folders" for components. They group components and can be added or removed using `events` to create custom game-play.

Here is an example:

<CodeHeader path="BP/entities/example.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:entity" />

```json
"component_groups": {

    //the name of the component group
    "minecraft:cat_persian": {

        //A list of valid components. Add as many as you like.
        "minecraft:variant": {
            "value": 6
        },
        "minecraft:physics": {}
    },

    //the name of a second component group
    "wiki:example_group": {
        "minecraft:type_family": {
            "family": [
                "wiki_is_awesome!"
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

All component groups are custom-created. You cannot use component groups from other entities in your entity.

In vanilla Minecraft entities, component groups are namespaced with `minecraft:`, like `minecraft:cat_persian` above. But it is important to remember that they are _not components_. When you create your component groups, you can use whatever name/namespace:name combination you want. For example, `wiki:example_group` above. [Here](/concepts/namespaces)'s more info on namespaces.

When a component is placed into a group, is it _not_ automatically added to your entity. It won't do anything at all until the group is added. When the group is added, the component will become active and start affecting the behavior of your entity. You can also have multiple component groups added at once.

## Events

Events are a special syntax for adding and removing component groups that can be called by components when certain criteria are met. By adding/removing groups, we can create dynamic behavior for our entities.

An example:

<CodeHeader path="BP/entities/example.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:entity/events" />

```json
"minecraft:ageable_grow_up": { //Name of the event
    "remove": { //list of component groups to remove
        "component_groups": [
            "minecraft:cat_baby"
        ]
    },
    "add": {
        "component_groups": [
            "minecraft:cat_adult" //list of component groups to add.
        ]
    }
},
```

Like component groups, events are 100% custom-created inside each entity. You cannot use events from other entities on your own. Do not be tempted to use `"minecraft:ageable_grow_up"` in your own entity. If you want grow-up functionality, you need to define the component groups and events yourself.

The only thing you can add/remove from an entity is `component groups`. As tempting as it is to try and add/remove components directly, this is not possible.

Events are activated inside of certain components when some criteria is met. Below is an example:

<CodeHeader path="BP/entities/example.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:entity" />

```json
"components": {
    "minecraft:interact": {
        "interactions": [
            {
                "on_interact": {
                    "filters": [
                        {
                            "test":"is_family",
                            "subject": "other",
                            "value": "player"
                        }
                    ],
                    "target": "self",
                    "event": "wiki:on_interact"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
},
"component_groups": {
    "wiki:interacted": {
        "minecraft:scale": {
            "value": 2
        }
    }
},
"events":{
    "wiki:on_interact":{
        "add": {
            "component_groups": [ "wiki:interacted" ]
        }
    }
}
```

Here, when the entity is interacted with by the player, it will activate the `"wiki:on_interact"` event. The event will then add the component group `"wiki:interacted"`. This will then apply the component `"minecraft:scale"`.

For a more in depth tutorial on what events can do check out our page on entity events.

<Button link="/entities/entity-events">Entity Events</Button>

## Vanilla Usage

Component groups and events are the primary tools that vanilla entities use to create custom and adaptable behavior. Here are some vanilla features that are created using component groups and events:

-   The zombie is programmed to turn into a `drowned` if it spends too long under the water.

-   The fox has two component groups `minecraft:fox_red` and `minecraft:fox_active` to have the two color variants depending on where they spawn.

-   The enderman will become aggressive to the player when looked at.
======= CUSTOM ENTITY
24-
25-Similarly to custom items, we can also make custom entities with many similar mechanics to the vanilla entities in the game. These entities can be incredibly powerful allowing you to make your own animals which can be bred and tamed or an aggressive mob that attacks anything it sees.
26-
27-Here we will make a ghost entity which will float, attack the player and drop our ectoplasm item on death.
28-
29-<WikiImage src="ghost_view.png" width="150" />
30-
31-Just like items, entities are made up of two parts:
32-
33--   The visuals (texture, name, animations, sounds)
34:-   The behaviors (movement, attacks)
35-
36-Differently though, we will need two main files for our entity called the _server_ file and the _client_ file which sit in our BP and RP respectively.
37-We will also need additional files to describe the geometry of our entity and its animations, but we will cover those in later sections.
38-
39:First, we will cover how to create an entity & define its behavior. Next, we will look at how to add the visuals.
40-
41-## Entity Behavior
42-
43:Like with items, we need a file to tell our entity how to behave which points an identifier to certain components which define behavior. This file will be very similar to our item behavior file except with a lot more components.
44-
45-We define our server file in our BP, under the `BP/entities` folder.
46-We will call this file `ghost.json`.
47-
48-This is a basic overview of the file:
49-
50-<CodeHeader path="BP/entities/ghost.json" />
51-
52-```json
53-{
54:    "format_version": "1.26.60",
55-    "minecraft:entity": {
56-        "description": { ... },
57:        "components": { ... }
58-    }
59-}
60-```
61-
62-Just like with the items, we have our format version and here we have `"minecraft:entity"` as this is an entity file. From now on we won't comment on the format version and recommend to use the version example that we give.
63-
64-For entities we have a little bit more information under `description`:
65-
66-<ExampleFile path="BP/entities/ghost.json" snippet="minecraft:entity/description" />
67-
68:The `identifier` key serves the same purpose, to point to which entity we are talking about.
69-The other keys determine what ways we can add the entity to our world:
70-
71--   `is_summonable` — Whether it can be summoned using the `/summon` command.
72:-   `is_spawnable` — Whether a spawn egg is registered for the entity.
73-
74-We recommend leaving the settings as they are here as any changes will make it harder to test your entity in game.
75-
76-### Components
77-
78:An entity has many more behaviors than an item, so we'll need to define more components for it.
79:Here, we will break down different types of components into groups and then look at them closer.
80:For more information about entity components, you can check out our page [here](/entities/entity-intro-bp).
81-
82-### Stat Components
83-
84:These are the components that you will generally have on every entity. This define some core attributes to your entity.
85-
86:<CodeHeader path="BP/entities/ghost.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:entity/components" />
87-
88-```json
89-"minecraft:type_family": {
90-    "family": ["wiki:ghost", "monster"]
91-},
92:"minecraft:health": {
93-    "value": 20,
94-    "max": 20
95-},
96-"minecraft:attack": {
97-    "damage": 3
98-},
99-"minecraft:movement": {
100-    "value": 0.2
101-},
102-"minecraft:collision_box": {
103-    "width": 0.8,
104-    "height": 1.8
105-},
106-"minecraft:loot": {
107-    "table": "loot_tables/wiki/entities/ghost.json"
108-}
109-```
110-
111:-   The components `minecraft:health` and `minecraft:attack` and `minecraft:movement` are straight forward and set the entities health, attack damage and movement speed.
112-
113--   The `minecraft:collision_box` component of an entity is the box within which the entity interacts with or collides with blocks or other entities, aligned to the bottom middle of the entity.
114-    This component also determines the area where the entity can be hit or interacted with.
115-
116:-   The `minecraft:type_family` components determines the family of the entity which is used to group entities in a similar category together.
117-
118-    For example `monster` includes zombies, skeletons and creepers.
119-    This allows us to be able to select all entities with the `monster` tag.
120-
121-    Since the ghost family is custom, we've given it the `wiki:` namespace to avoid conflicts with other add-ons that may add their own ghosts with a similar family.
122-
123--   The `minecraft:loot` component defines the path to the loot table that the entity will drop on death. We will create this loot table in a later section using this path.
124-
125-### Movement Components
126-
127-In order for an entity to move around, we need to define two things, _how_ it moves and _where_ it can move to.
128:This is defined using the `movement` and `navigation` components respectively.
129-
130-You will always need a `movement` and `navigation` component if you want your entity to be able to move.
131-
132:<CodeHeader path="BP/entities/ghost.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:entity/components" />
133-
134-```json
135-"minecraft:physics": {},
136-"minecraft:jump.static": {},
137-"minecraft:movement.basic": {},
138-"minecraft:navigation.walk": {
139-    "can_walk": true,
140-    "avoid_sun": true,
141-    "can_pass_doors": true,
142-    "can_open_doors": true
143-}
144-```
145-
146--   `minecraft:physics` is used to apply gravity and collision to your entity. Note: you cannot change this component using component groups.
147--   `minecraft:jump.static` allows your entity to jump up blocks for traversal. Both are used on almost every entity.
148-
149:There are few different types of movement components which allow different types of movement such as `minecraft:movement.swim` used by dolphins, `minecraft:movement.fly` used by parrots and `minecraft:movement.hover` used by bees.
150-
151--   The `minecraft:movement.basic` component allows our entity to walk by moving over blocks.
152-    To make it seem like our entity is actually floating, we will use our geometry.
153-
154--   The `minecraft:navigation.walk` component is a pathfinder which defines what paths we allow our entity to follow.
155-    For example skeletons will try not to walk in sunlight, so their pathing stops them from taking paths that would put them in sunlight.
156-    Additionally, parrots can fly so they can path into the air unlike walking mobs.
157-
158:These components have a lot of different settings which allow for interesting pathing.
159-The settings we've chosen let our ghost walk along the ground, avoid stepping into sunlight, pass through doorways and open doors.
160-
161-### Behavior Components
162-
163-While we have defined _how_ our entity does things, we haven't yet defined _when_ or _what_ they do.
164:This is where `behavior` (also known as AI goal) components come in.
165:These components define the specific actions that our entity will do.
166-
167:For example, villagers will try to breed since they have the `minecraft:behavior.breed` component and tamed wolves follow their owners since they have the `minecraft:behavior.follow_owner` component.
168-
169:We want our ghost to be able to idly walk and look around, target the player when nearby and then attack them. Here are the components that we use:
170-
171:<CodeHeader path="BP/entities/ghost.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:entity/components" />
172-
173-```json
174-// Allow for random movement and looking around
175:"minecraft:behavior.random_stroll": { ... },
176:"minecraft:behavior.random_look_around": { ... },
177:"minecraft:behavior.look_at_player": { ... },
178-// Allow for targeting
179:"minecraft:behavior.hurt_by_target": { ... },
180:"minecraft:behavior.nearest_attackable_target": { ... },
181-// Allow for attacking
182:"minecraft:behavior.delayed_attack": { ... }
183-```
184-
185:The first component, `minecraft:behavior.random_stroll` allows our entity to choose a random point nearby to path to periodically.
186-This path is created with our `navigation` component and then the type of movement is defined by our `movement` component.
187-
188:The next two components allow our entity to randomly look around and to look at the player if they are within range.
189-
190-For attacking, in order for our entity to attack, it needs a `target`.
191:The two behaviors `minecraft:behavior.hurt_by_target` and `minecraft:behavior.nearest_attackable_target` will cause the entity to target any entity that hurts it and target any the nearest enemy to it within range.
192-
193:Finally, the `minecraft:behavior.delayed_attack` is how our entity actually attacks it target.
194-
195:Each of these behaviors have further settings to tweak the exact behavior we want.
196-
197:<CodeHeader path="BP/entities/ghost.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:entity/components" />
198-
199-```json
200-// Allow for random movement and looking around
201:"minecraft:behavior.random_stroll": {
202-    "priority": 6,
203-    "speed_multiplier": 1
204-},
205:"minecraft:behavior.random_look_around": {
206-    "priority": 7
207-},
208:"minecraft:behavior.look_at_player": {
209-    "priority": 7,
210-    "look_distance": 6,
211-    "probability": 0.02
212-},
213-// Allow for targeting
214:"minecraft:behavior.hurt_by_target": {
215-    "priority": 1
216-},
217:"minecraft:behavior.nearest_attackable_target": {
218-    "priority": 2,
219-    "within_radius": 25,
220-    "reselect_targets": true,
221-    "entity_types": [
222-        {
223-            "filters": {
224-                "any_of": [
225-                    {
226-                        "test": "is_family",
227-                        "subject": "other",
228-                        "value": "player"
229-                    }
230-                ]
231-            },
232-            "max_dist": 35
233-        }
234-    ]
235-},
236-// Allow for attacking
237:"minecraft:behavior.delayed_attack": {
238-    "priority": 0,
239-    "attack_once": false,
240-    "track_target": true,
241-    "require_complete_path": false,
242-    "random_stop_interval": 0,
243-    "reach_multiplier": 1.5,
244-    "speed_multiplier": 1,
245-    "attack_duration": 0.75,
246-    "hit_delay_pct": 0.5
247-}
248-```
249-
250-For more details about what each of these options do, you can read about them on the official documentation, [bedrock.dev](https://bedrock.dev/docs/stable/Entities).
251-
252-#### Priority
253-
254:All behaviors contain a `"priority"` field. This field is used to decide which behavior to run when many can.
255-
256:When the entity is picking something to do, it searches all its behaviors from lowest priority to the highest priority and picks the first one that it can do. For this reason, you need to make important behaviors like `minecraft:behavior.nearest_attackable_target` lower than behaviors like `minecraft:behavior.look_at_player`. If the `look_at_player` behavior is lower, it will always run this first when the player is close, and the entity will never attack.
257-
258:In general, important behaviors will have a priority of `0` or `1`.
259-
260-### Full Entity Behavior File
261-
262-<Spoiler title="Full ghost.json">
263-
264-<ExampleFile path="BP/entities/ghost.json" />
265-
266-</Spoiler>
267-
268:With that we have completed our entity behavior file.
269-
270-More complex entities can also have different _states_, where they will behave differently depending on what state they are in. For example, a wild wolf will walk around freely, but once it is tamed it will follow the player. An _event_ (being tamed) caused the wolf to change _states_. This feature allows us to create dynamic entities which can perform different actions when different events occurs. You can learn more about this in our guide [here](/entities/entity-intro-bp).
271-
272-If you open your world and try to summon in your entity using `/summon wiki:ghost`, it should behave like we expect but there will only be a shadow on the ground. You might also see its name as a translation key, similar to how it happened with our item.
273-
274-Next we will learn how to create our resource or client file and how to assign our texture, geometry and animations.
275-
276-## Entity Resources
277-
278-Applying visuals to an entity is very different to an item. Since there are a lot more pieces, we have a separate file dedicated to defining the resources.
279-This is the called entity _client file_ which we will name `ghost.entity.json`. These files go in the folder `RP/entity`.
280-
281-In this section, we will use the example resources created for our ghost entity to demonstrate how to add them to an entity. In the next section of the guide, we explain how to use Blockbench, a dedicated 3D editor, to create your own entity geometry and animations.
282-
283-### Model
284-
285-The 'model' for our entity is the shape of our entity, also called the 'geometry'.
286-This describes the visual shape of our entity, like how a pig is a box with 4 legs and a head whereas a chicken has 2 legs, a head and wings.
287-The geometry is stored as a JSON file in the `RP/models/entity` folder and ours will be named `ghost.geo.json`.
288-
289-This file is automatically generated by Blockbench for us, so there is no need to learn or modify its JSON format by hand.
290-As such, we won't go into full detail when looking at the file. It stores the data about each block in our model, such as size, position and rotation.
291-
292-<ExampleFile path="RP/models/entity/ghost.geo.json" />
293-
294:The important information that we need is the `identifier` which we will use to reference our geometry file, which here is `geometry.ghost`.
295-
296-### Texture
297-
298-Our entity now has its shape, but it also needs a texture.
299-This texture can also be created in Blockbench and is simply a `.png` file.
300-
301-<ExampleFile path="RP/textures/wiki/entity/ghost.png" />
302-
303-You may recall, when we made our item, we assigned a shortname to our texture to reference later.
304-We will be doing something similar for our entity within our entity file, so make sure you keep the file path to the texture.
305-
306-### Animations
307-
308-Animations allow our entity to have more life and move in different ways.
309-We can have as many animations for an entity as we want and we can also trigger them at different types using an _animation controller_ which we will cover in the next section.
310-
311-Depending on your entity, you may want different animations.
312-For our ghost we will have an `idle`, `attack` and `move` animation.
313-These files are also created automatically in Blockbench, so we won't look into it in full detail.
314-
315-An animation file can contain one or multiple animations within it. Our animations will all be under one file called `ghost.animations.json` inside the `RP/animations` folder.
316-
317-<CodeHeader path="RP/animations/ghost.animations.json" />
318-

322-    "animations": {

158:### Cooldown
159-
160-Determines how cooldowns are triggered for the item and how long each cooldown should last.
161-
162-_Requires format version [1.20.10](/items/item-format-history#_1-20-10) or later._
163-
164-#### Object Format {#cooldown-object}
165-
166--   `category` — String
167-    -   The category of cooldown for this item.
168-    -   Items with the same category will share cooldowns.
169--   `duration` — Float
170-    -   The duration of time (in seconds) items with a matching category will spend cooling down before becoming usable again.
171-    -   If this value is a negative number, it renders the item unusable.
172--   `type` — String (optional)
173-    -   Determines which of the following types of input the cooldown affects:
174-        -   `"use"`{lang=json} (default) causes the cooldown to start when the item is used and prevents the item from being used while the cooldown is active.
175-        -   `"attack"`{lang=json} causes the cooldown to start when the player attacks while holding the item and prevents the item from being used to attack while the cooldown is active.
176-
177-<CodeHeader breadcrumbs="minecraft:item/components" />
178-
179-```json
180-"minecraft:cooldown": {
181-    "category": "wiki:cooldown",
182-    "duration": 0.2,
183-    "type": "use"
184-}
185-```
186-
187:### Damage
188-
189-Determines how much extra damage (`0-32767`{lang=js}) the item deals on attack, displaying as "+X Attack Damage" in the item's tooltip.
190-
191-_Requires format version [1.26.0](/items/item-format-history#_1-26-0) or later._
192-
193-#### Integer Format {#damage-integer}

196-

198-"minecraft:damage": 10
199-```

201:### Damage Absorption
202-
203-Causes the item to absorb damage that would otherwise be dealt to its wearer.
204-For this to happen, the item needs to have the durability component and be equipped in an armor slot.
205-
206-_Requires format version [1.21.20](/items/item-format-history#_1-21-20) or later._
207-
208-#### Object Format {#damage-absorption-object}
209-
210--   `absorbable_causes` — Array
211-    -   List of damage causes (such as `entity_attack` and `magma`) that can be absorbed by the item.
212-    -   See the autocompletion for the `/damage` command for a list of available damage causes.
213-
214-<CodeHeader breadcrumbs="minecraft:item/components" />
215-
216-```json
217-"minecraft:damage_absorption": {
218-    "absorbable_causes": ["all"]
219-}
220-```

222-### Digger
223-
224-Determine how quickly an item can dig specific blocks.
225-
226-_Requires format version [1.20.20](/items/item-format-history#_1-20-20) or later._
227-
228-#### Object Format {#digger-object}
229-
230--   `destroy_speeds` — Array
231-    -   `block` — [Block Descriptor](/documentation/shared-constructs#block-descriptors)
232-        -   The block that the related destroy speed will apply to.
233-    -   `speed` — Integer
234-        -   The speed at which the block will be mined.
235-        -   When `0`{lang=json}, the item will not be able to destroy the block.
236--   `use_efficiency` — Boolean (optional)
--
288:### Durability
289-
290-Allows the item to take damage and determines how much damage the item can take before breaking.
291-
292--   Allows the durability of the item to be combined with another item of the same type via crafting.
293--   Even if the item is a [digger](#digger), it will not be damaged when mining blocks.
294--   Each time an entity is hit using this item, the item's damage increases by 2.
295-    This does not match vanilla damage for weapons, but does match vanilla damage for tools.
296--   When the item is [wearable](#wearable), hitting an entity will not damage the item.
297-    Instead, it implicitly increments the damage when worn and the entity is hurt.
298-
299-_Requires format version [1.20.0](/items/item-format-history#_1-20-0) or later._
300-
301-#### Object Format {#durability-object}
302-
303--   `damage_chance` — Integer [Range](/documentation/shared-constructs#range-objects) (optional)
304-    -   Determines the percentage chance range of the item receiving damage when it has the "Unbreaking" enchantment.
305-    -   When the item does not have the "Unbreaking" enchantment, it is damaged 100% of the time regardless of this range.
306-    -   When the item has the "Unbreaking" enchantment, its chance of being damaged is as follows:
307-        -   Unbreaking I — 50% of the range.
308-        -   Unbreaking II — 33% of the range.
309-        -   Unbreaking III — 25% of the range.
310--   `max_durability` — Integer (`0-32767`{lang=js}) ([MCPE-180112](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE-180112))
311-    -   The amount of damage that the item can take before breaking.
312-
313-<CodeHeader breadcrumbs="minecraft:item/components" />
314-
315-```json
316-"minecraft:durability": {
317-    "damage_chance": {
318-        "min": 0,
319-        "max": 100
320-    },
321-    "max_durability": 238
322-}
323-```
--
325:### Durability Sensor
326-
327-Allows an item to trigger effects when it receives damage.
328-
329-_Requires format version [1.26.50](/items/item-format-history#_1-26-50) or later._
330-
331-#### Object Format {#durability-sensor-object}
332-
333--   `durability_thresholds` — Array
334-    -   Items define both the durability thresholds, and the effects emitted when each threshold is met.
335-    -   When multiple thresholds are met, only the threshold with the lowest durability after applying the damage is considered.
336-    -   `durability` — Integer
337-        -   The effects are emitted when the item durability value is less than or equal to this value.
338-    -   `particle_type` — String (optional)
339-        -   Vanilla particle type to spawn when the threshold is met.
340-    -   `sound_event` — String (optional)
341-        -   Vanilla level sound event or `RP/sounds/sound_definitions.json` entry to trigger when the threshold is met.
342-
343-<CodeHeader breadcrumbs="minecraft:item/components" />
344-
345-```json
346-"minecraft:durability_sensor": {
347-    "durability_thresholds": [
348-        {
349-            "durability": 100,
350-            "particle_type": "minecraft:explosion_manual",
351-            "sound_event": "blast"
352-        },
353-        {
354-            "durability": 5,
355-            "sound_event": "raid.horn"
356-        }
357-    ]
358-}
359-```

507:### Food
508-
509-Allows the item to be consumed when used by players.
510-
511--   The item must also have the [`minecraft:use_modifiers`](#use-modifiers) with a defined `use_duration` component in order to function properly.
512--   To display an eating/drinking animation, also apply the [`minecraft:use_animation`](#use-animation) component to the item.
513-
514-:::danger CAN ALWAYS EAT ([MCPE-178647](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE-178647), [MCPE-188410](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE-188410))
515-Custom items can always be eaten when the player is full even when `can_always_eat` is set to `false`{lang=json}.

832:### Rarity
833-
834-Represents how difficult the item is to obtain by changing the color of its name text.
835-This component will be overridden and have no effect if the `minecraft:hover_text_color` is also applied.
836-
837-An item's rarity value will be upgraded to `rare` if enchanted, or `epic` if its base rarity is already `rare`.

111--   The components `minecraft:health` and `minecraft:attack` and `minecraft:movement` are straight forward and set the entities health, attack damage and movement speed.

113:-   The `minecraft:collision_box` component of an entity is the box within which the entity interacts with or collides with blocks or other entities, aligned to the bottom middle of the entity.
114-    This component also determines the area where the entity can be hit or interacted with.
115-

118-    For example `monster` includes zombies, skeletons and creepers.

123:The weight is the chance of this entry being chosen. The higher the weight in comparison to other entries in this "entries" array, the higher the chance of the entry being chosen.
124-
125-```json
126-"weight": 3
127-```
128-
129-###### Quality
130-
131-The weight of an entry can be changed based on the player's luck using the quality property.
132-
133-```json
134-"quality": 2
135-```
136-
137-Currently, luck is only expressed when fishing with a fishing rod enchanted with Luck of the Sea.

139-#### Tiered Pools
140-
141:Tiered pools are used to select exactly one entry from a collection.
142-
143-```json
144-{
145-    "tiers": {
146-        "initial_range": 2,
147-
148:        "bonus_rolls": 3,
149-        "bonus_chance": 0.095
150-    },
151-
152:    "entries": [
153-        {
154-            "type": "loot_table",
155-            "name": "loot_tables/entities/armor_set_leather.json"
156-        },
157-        {
158-            "type": "loot_table",
159-            "name": "loot_tables/entities/armor_set_gold.json"
160-        },
161-        {
162-            "type": "loot_table",
163-            "name": "loot_tables/entities/armor_set_chain.json"
164-        },
165-        {
166-            "type": "loot_table",
167-            "name": "loot_tables/entities/armor_set_iron.json"
168-        },
169-        {
170-            "type": "loot_table",
171-            "name": "loot_tables/entities/armor_set_diamond.json"
172-        }
173-    ]
174-}
175-```
176-
177-A pool becomes tiered with the inclusion of the `"tiers"` object property:
178-
179-```json
180-"tiers": {
181-	"initial_range": 2,
182-
183:	"bonus_rolls": 3,
184-	"bonus_chance": 0.095
185-}
186-```
187-
188:Entries in a tiered pool are _ordered_. The selected entry for a tiered pool is based on its index. To determine this index, a starting index is randomly rolled and then a batch of success rolls attempt to increment this starting index.
189-
190-The starting index is decided by rolling a random integer between 1 and the integer property `"initial_range"`. If no initial range is provided, it defaults to `1`, forcing a starting index of 1.
191-
192:Next, attempts are made to advanced the index using additional rolls. The count of these roll attempts is given as an integer to `"bonus_rolls"`. The chance that any such roll succeeds is given via `"bonus_chance"`. Chances for `"bonus_chance"` are out of 1, meaning `0.5` would be a 50% chance for any bonus roll to succeed. Each successful roll increases the index by 1. Both of these properties default to `0`, meaning both must be provided to use this additional rolls mechanic.
193-
194:The final determined index is used to select the corresponding entry as that pool's yield. Indices in tiered pools are one-indexed, meaning the first entry has an index of 1, the second has an index of 2, and so forth. If the determined index is larger than the entry count for that pool, no yield will be provided.
195-
196-::: warning
197:All [conditions](#) on entries in a tiered pool are ignored. Conditions on the pool itself are still allowed.
198-:::

201-
202:Entries are the selectable units of a pool. Three different types of entries are available.
203-

205-
206:Item entries are the fundamental entry type for selecting loot. Item entries refer to
207-

209-"type": "item",
210-"name": "minecraft:apple",
211-"weight": 1

225-
226:When selected, empty entries won't yield any loot for that roll.
227-

230-"weight": 4
231-```
232-
233:Empty entries can generally be mimicked using [a roll count](#) whose range includes 0, [random chance conditions](#), or [count functions](#) that could randomly select 0. Their primary advantage is readability when using [weighted random pools](#): denoting by weight when a roll won't yield an entry may be easier to understand.

View [item functions](/loot/item-functions) for a full list of functions and how they're used.

694-### Liquid Detection
695-
696-Determines how this blocks behaves with different types of liquid.

698-_Requires format version [1.26.0](/blocks/block-format-history#_1-26-0) or later._
699-
700-#### Object Format {#liquid-detection-object}
701-
702--   `detection_rules` — Array
703-    -   `liquid_type` — String
704-        -   Which type of liquid this rule applies to. Currently only `"water"`{lang=json} is supported.
705-    -   `can_contain_liquid` — Boolean
706-        -   Whether the liquid type can occupy the same space as this block e.g., [waterlogging](/blocks/block-colocation#waterlogging).
707-    -   `on_liquid_touches` — String (optional)
708-        -   Determines what happens when the liquid type flows into the block based on one of the following values:
709-            -   `"blocking"`{lang=json} (default) prevents the liquid from flowing.
710-            -   `"broken"`{lang=json} causes the block to be broken.
711-            -   `"no_reaction"`{lang=json} allows the liquid to flow through the block.
712-            -   `"popped"`{lang=json} causes the block to be popped off, dropping its loot.
713-    -   `stops_liquid_flowing_from_direction` — Array (optional)
714-        -   Determines an array of directions that the liquid cannot flow out of this block from.
715-        -   If `on_liquid_touches` is set to `"no_reaction"`{lang=json}, this array also determines the directions that the liquid cannot flow into this block from.
716-    -   `use_liquid_clipping` — Boolean (optional)
717-        -   Determines whether liquid contained in the block is visually clipped based on the block's encompassing collider (the smallest box containing all [collision boxes](#collision-box)).
718-        -   By default, liquid is not clipped.

789:### Material Instances
790-
791-Defines the [material instances](/blocks/block-visuals-intro#material-instances) of a block, configuring how parts of the block are rendered.
792-
793-_Requires format version [1.26.20](/blocks/block-format-history#_1-26-20) or later._
794-
795-**Known Issues:**
796-
797--   In user interfaces, face dimming is applied before rotation from `item_display_transforms` in the block model ([MCPE-235788](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE-235788)).
798--   PBR textures are not supported by custom blocks when rendered as entities (when held, in item frames, on ground, etc.) ([MCPE-237517](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE-237517)).
799-
800-#### Object Format {#material-instances-object}
801-
802-Each key is the name of a material instance and each value is a material instance object.
803-The `*` instance is the default instance for all cube faces, however it is not required if all faces have a material instance separately defined.
804-
805--   `<name>`{lang=xml} — Object
806-    -   `texture` — String
807-        -   Specifies the [texture atlas](/concepts/texture-atlases) shortname to use from `RP/textures/terrain_texture.json`.
808-    -   `render_method` — String (optional)
809-        -   The [render method](/blocks/block-visuals-intro#render-methods) to use when rendering faces using the material instance.
810-        -   **All material instances must use the same render method.**
811-        -   By default, the `opaque` render method is used.
812-    -   `tint_method` — String (optional)
813-        -   Specifies the [tint method](/blocks/block-tinting#tint-methods) used to tint the `texture` based on the biome the block is placed in.
814-    -   `alpha_masked_tint` — Boolean (optional)
815-        -   Determines whether the intensity of the tint applied by tint methods should be based on the alpha channel of the texture.
816-        -   When `true`{lang=json}, a `tint_method` must be specified (that is not `"none"`{lang=json}) and the `render_method` must be `"opaque"`{lang=json}.
817-        -   By default, tinting from tint methods is not alpha-masked.
818-    -   `ambient_occlusion` — Float (`0.0-10.0`{lang=json}) (optional)
819-        -   Determines the intensity of "smooth lighting" that is applied to faces using the material instance.
820-        -   By default, this is or `0.0`{lang=json} for blocks that emit light and `1.0`{lang=json} for blocks that do not emit light.
821-    -   `face_dimming` — Boolean (optional)
822-        -   Determines whether faces using the material instance are dimmed by their direction.
823-        -   By default, this is `false`{lang=json} for blocks that emit light and `true`{lang=json} for blocks that do not emit light.
824-    -   `isotropic` — Boolean (optional)
825-        -   Determines whether the UVs of faces using the material instance are randomly rotated based on the block's position in the world.
826-        -   By default, textures are not randomly rotated.

- East (right side) at (u, v+d), size d×h
- North (front) at (u+d, v+d), size w×h
- West (left) at (u+d+w, v+d), size d×h
- South (back) at (u+d+w+d, v+d), size w×h
- Up at (u+d, v), size w×d

14-description: Spawn rules define how entities will spawn into the world.

17-Spawn rules define how entities will spawn into the world. You should use spawn rules when you want your custom entity to spawn naturally, just like vanilla entities. The different components allow you to define when, where, and how the entity will spawn in.
18-
19:In general, it's possible to spawn your custom entity in a very similar way as vanilla entities. e.g, in a herd like a cow, only at night like a vanilla zombie, or only underwater like a fish.

75--   "`description`">"`identifier`": the entity to spawn
76:-   "`population_control`": controls spawning and despawning quantities. Can be set to "`animal`", "`underwater_animal`", "`monster`" and "`ambient`".
77:-   "`conditions`" are a list of conditions that have to be met in order for the spawn attempt to succeed.
78--   "`minecraft:spawns_on_surface`", "`minecraft:spawns_underground`" and "`minecraft:spawns_underwater`" control where the entity spawns cap-wise.
79:-   "`minecraft_brightness_filter`" can be set from 0 to 15 and controls in which light levels can entities spawn. - "`adjust_for_weather`" defines whether it light levels are counted lower during rain or thunder weather.
80--   "`minecraft:difficulty_filter`" sets the range of level difficulty to enable this entity's spawns.
81:-   "`minecraft:herd`" sets the number of entities spawning together, on the same spawn rule.
82:-   "`minecraft:permute_type`" with "`weight`"s and "`entity_type`"s sets a chance for the spawned entity to mutate into a different one.
83:-   "`minecraft:biome_filter`" tests for certain biome tags. Look up the filter syntax and list of biome tags in the documentation or search examples in the vanilla Example pack.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Crear una aplicación en español para diseñar y generar automáticamente addons completos de Minecraft Bedrock reciente, exportables como `.mcaddon`.
- Permitir crear objetos, bloques y criaturas, con la meta expresada por el usuario de que los addons sean “mejores que el action stuff”.

## Requirements
- Trabajar sobre el proyecto existente y asumir lo que falte sin hacer preguntas.
- Integrar IA para generar addons automáticamente y procurar compatibilidad con la versión más reciente de Bedrock.
- Interfaz para crear objetos, bloques y criaturas.

## Decisions
- Aplicación web con diseñador, biblioteca de contenido, vista previa de archivos y plantillas.
- Persistir proyectos en `localStorage` y generar paquetes de comportamiento y recursos al exportar.
- Se añadió un motor local sin conexión como base para interpretar descripciones y normalizar especificaciones; su versión declarada es `1.26.60`. La integración con un servicio externo de IA aún está por confirmar.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `styles.css` y `app.js` implementan la aplicación, la interfaz en español, el diseñador, la biblioteca, las plantillas, el almacenamiento local y la exportación.
- Se ajustó la generación de objetos, alimentos y criaturas; el idioma generado usa `es_ES`.
- Se creó `ai-engine.js` con generación local de especificaciones para objetos, bloques y criaturas, saneamiento de respuestas externas y límites de datos.

### Active
- Integrar y verificar `ai-engine.js` con la aplicación existente y comprobar la experiencia de generación automática.
- Validar sintaxis e integración, probar creación, plantillas, filtros, eliminación, archivos y exportación `.mcaddon`.
- Revisar la interfaz en navegador y validar la estructura y los JSON exportados.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Ejecutar `node --check app.js` y `node --check ai-engine.js`; comprobar cómo se cargan e invocan los scripts desde `index.html`.
2. Integrar el motor de IA donde corresponda y probar generación para objetos, bloques y criaturas.
3. Probar los flujos de la aplicación en navegador y validar el `.mcaddon` exportado y sus JSON.
4. Informar al terminar de los supuestos y del alcance real de la compatibilidad; no afirmar que el addon sea jugable o sin errores sin verificarlo.

## Relevant Files
- `ai-engine.js`: motor local de generación y saneamiento de contenido.
- `app.js`: estado de la aplicación, generación de archivos Bedrock y exportación.
- `index.html`: interfaz y carga de scripts.
- `styles.css`: estilos y diseño adaptable.
- `README.md`: metadatos del proyecto.

## Important Context
- Los cambios no están confirmados en Git.
- La última validación conocida de `app.js` ocurrió antes de las ediciones recientes; `ai-engine.js` aún no se ha validado ni probado.
- La app cargó previamente en Chromium; solo se observó un 404 de `favicon.ico`. No se ha comprobado que el `.mcaddon` exportado sea válido o jugable.
- Las búsquedas web sobre documentación y versión actual fueron canceladas; se consultaron páginas de Bedrock Wiki, incluida `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bedrock-OSS/bedrock-wiki/wiki/docs/guide/custom-entity.md`.

289-
290-Allows the item to take damage and determines how much damage the item can take before breaking.
291-
292--   Allows the durability of the item to be combined with another item of the same type via crafting.
293--   Even if the item is a [digger](#digger), it will not be damaged when mining blocks.
294--   Each time an entity is hit using this item, the item's damage increases by 2.
295-    This does not match vanilla damage for weapons, but does match vanilla damage for tools.
296--   When the item is [wearable](#wearable), hitting an entity will not damage the item.
297-    Instead, it implicitly increments the damage when worn and the entity is hurt.
298-

301-#### Object Format {#durability-object}
302-
303--   `damage_chance` — Integer [Range](/documentation/shared-constructs#range-objects) (optional)
304-    -   Determines the percentage chance range of the item receiving damage when it has the "Unbreaking" enchantment.
305-    -   When the item does not have the "Unbreaking" enchantment, it is damaged 100% of the time regardless of this range.
306-    -   When the item has the "Unbreaking" enchantment, its chance of being damaged is as follows:
307-        -   Unbreaking I — 50% of the range.
308-        -   Unbreaking II — 33% of the range.
309-        -   Unbreaking III — 25% of the range.
310--   `max_durability` — Integer (`0-32767`{lang=js}) ([MCPE-180112](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE-180112))
311-    -   The amount of damage that the item can take before breaking.

Here, the shortname references the sound shortname defined in the `sound_definitions.json` file. When using the sound elsewhere, such as in a command, you would use `mob.entity.attack_1`, but in an animation defined in the entity, you would use `attack_1`.

## Particle Effects

Particle effects are files which contain information about the movement of many small spires to create effects like smoke or fire. Similarly to sound effects, this key defines short names for particle effects to be used in animations. For example, the phantom has particle effects on its wings as it flies around.

<CodeHeader path="RP/entity/example.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:client_entity/description" />

```json
"particle_effects": {
    "smoke": "wiki:smoke_particle"
}
```

Here, the shortname references the identifier for the particle. For more information on particles and making your own, check out our particle pages [here](/particles/particles). For more information on using sound effects and particle effect in animations you can also check out our page [here](/visuals/animation-effects).

## Spawn Egg

The spawn egg key allows us to generate a spawn egg for our entity. When used this will spawn in our entity and is automatically added to the creative inventory. There are two options for the look of your spawn egg, colored and texture.

<CodeHeader path="RP/entity/example.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:client_entity/description" />

```json
"spawn_egg": {
    "base_color": "#db7500",
    "overlay_color": "#242222"
}
```

Using `base_color` and `overlay_color` will create a texture egg similar to the vanilla ones with the colors provided.

<CodeHeader path="RP/entity/example.json" breadcrumbs="minecraft:client_entity/description" />

```json
"spawn_egg": {
    "texture": "wiki:example",
}
```

The `texture` key takes the texture shortname of an image, defined in `item_texture.json`, to use as the image for the spawn egg. If this key is omitted, then a spawn egg will not be generated.

## Additional Settings

`enable_attachables` determines whether or not attachables can be attached to the entity. For example, setting this to false means that the entity cannot hold weapons like swords or bows.

`hide_armor` allows the entity to wear armor, but it will not be rendered.

### Modifying the Player Client Entity

In order to support persona skins (created in the Character Creator), the `min_engine_version` of the client entity definition cannot be greater than 1.13.0.
Ensure that you include the following parameter in the player client entity file:

<CodeHeader path="RP/entity/player.entity.json" />

```json
{
    "format_version": "1.26.60",
    "minecraft:client_entity": {
        "description": {
            "identifier": "minecraft:player",
            "min_engine_version": "1.13.0",
            ...
        }
    }
}
```

## Objective
- Crear una aplicación en español para diseñar addons completos de Minecraft Bedrock, con objetos, bloques y criaturas, y exportarlos como `.mcaddon`.
- Hacer que la generación automática produzca addons de calidad, sin afirmar compatibilidad o jugabilidad no verificadas.

## Requirements
- Trabajar sobre el proyecto existente y resolver por cuenta propia los detalles faltantes.
- Ofrecer generación automática por IA y una interfaz para crear objetos, bloques y criaturas.
- Procurar compatibilidad con Bedrock reciente y validar los archivos generados.

## Decisions
- Aplicación web con diseñador, biblioteca, plantillas, vista previa de archivos y persistencia en `localStorage`.
- Se añadió un motor local como respaldo de generación y se integró una opción de IA en la nube, API compatible con OpenAI u Ollama.
- La exportación genera paquetes de comportamiento y recursos, texturas procedurales y un `.mcaddon` ZIP.

## Work State
### Completed
- `ai-engine.js` contiene generación local y saneamiento de respuestas externas; se corrigieron detección de criaturas/bloques y normalización de identificadores y respuestas JSON.
- `app.js` fue reemplazado por una implementación que genera JSON de objetos, bloques, criaturas, recetas, loot, manifest, texturas procedurales y archivo `.mcaddon`.
- `index.html` recibió una sección de generación por IA y una nota de comportamiento para bloques y criaturas.

### Active
- Integrar y comprobar la interfaz completa, la generación local/externa y las plantillas.
- Validar JSON Bedrock, manifiestos, referencias de texturas y modelos, recetas y reglas de aparición.
- Probar filtros, eliminación, persistencia, vista previa de archivos y exportación `.mcaddon` en navegador.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Ejecutar `node --check app.js` y `node --check ai-engine.js`; comprobar carga de ambos scripts en `index.html`.
2. Revisar la interfaz y corregir el fallo de edición de plantillas: el intento de añadir las plantillas `sword` y `entity` no se aplicó porque no coincidió el texto objetivo.
3. Probar generación para objetos, bloques y criaturas, tanto local como externa; comprobar que API y respaldo funcionen como se indica.
4. Inspeccionar los archivos exportados y validar los JSON y referencias; probar importación/jugabilidad en Bedrock si es posible.
5. Aclarar y unificar la versión objetivo: `app.js` usa `FORMAT_VERSION = '1.21.90'` y `MIN_ENGINE = [1, 21, 90]`, mientras que el motor local declara `1.26.60`.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: generación de contenido, JSON Bedrock, texturas, IA y exportación.
- `ai-engine.js`: generación local y saneamiento de contenido externo.
- `index.html`: interfaz y carga de scripts.
- `styles.css`: estilos de la aplicación.
- `README.md`: metadatos y descripción del proyecto.

## Important Context
- Los cambios siguen sin confirmarse en Git; el repositorio muestra archivos sin seguimiento, incluidos `app.js`, `ai-engine.js`, `index.html` y `styles.css`.
- La búsqueda web de documentación y versión actual fue cancelada; se consultaron páginas de Bedrock Wiki y muestras de Mojang, pero la exportación nueva no está verificada.
- Pollinations se probó con una solicitud de ejemplo; no se ha probado su integración completa desde la aplicación.
- Una inspección previa de `ai-engine.js` encontró clasificaciones incorrectas de criaturas y bloques; se editaron esas reglas, pero no se han vuelto a ejecutar las pruebas de generación.
- La edición de plantillas falló con `Could not find oldString in .../index.html`; las plantillas de espada y criatura aún no se han añadido.

-   Configures which `menu_category` the block is placed into.
    -   Also takes the optional parameters `group` and `is_hidden_in_commands`.

_The block description is also home to [states](/blocks/block-states) and [traits](/blocks/block-traits), which are covered in their own pages._

## Adding Components

Right now, our custom block is using the default component values (which can be found [here](/blocks/block-components)).

Let's configure our own functionality!

<CodeHeader path="BP/blocks/custom_block.json" />

```json
{
    "format_version": "1.26.60",
    "minecraft:block": {
        "description": {
            "identifier": "wiki:custom_block",
            "menu_category": {
                "category": "construction"
            }
        },
        "components": {
            "minecraft:destructible_by_mining": {
                "seconds_to_destroy": 3
            },
            "minecraft:destructible_by_explosion": {
                "explosion_resistance": 3
            },
            "minecraft:map_color": "#ffffff",
            "minecraft:light_dampening": 0,
            "minecraft:light_emission": 4,
            "minecraft:loot": "loot_tables/blocks/custom_block.json"
        }
    }
}
```

-   [`minecraft:destructible_by_mining`](/blocks/block-components#destructible-by-mining) defines how long the player will need to mine the block until it breaks. Currently, it isn't possible to set different destroy times for different tools.
-   [`minecraft:destructible_by_explosion`](/blocks/block-components#destructible-by-explosion) defines the resistance to explosions. The higher the value, the lower the chance of destruction.
-   [`minecraft:map_color`](/blocks/block-components#map-color) is the hex color code that will be displayed on a Minecraft map to represent this block. `"#ffffff"`{lang=json} means white. You can get hex codes for other colors [here](https://www.google.com/search?q=hex+color+picker).
-   [`minecraft:light_dampening`](/blocks/block-components#light-dampening) defines how much light will be blocked from passing through.
-   [`minecraft:light_emission`](/blocks/block-components#light-emission) defines the light level the block will output.
-   [`minecraft:loot`](/blocks/block-components#loot) defines a loot table path for the block to drop. If this is removed, then the block will drop itself. You can learn more about loot tables [here](/loot/loot-tables).

_Browse more block components [here](/blocks/block-components)!_

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Crear una aplicación en español para diseñar addons de Minecraft Bedrock con objetos, bloques y criaturas, y exportarlos como `.mcaddon`.
- Hacer que la generación automática y la edición manual produzcan archivos útiles, sin afirmar compatibilidad o jugabilidad no verificadas.

## Requirements
- Trabajar sobre el proyecto existente y resolver detalles faltantes.
- Ofrecer generación por IA y una interfaz para crear objetos, bloques y criaturas.
- Procurar compatibilidad con Bedrock reciente y validar los archivos generados.

## Decisions
- Aplicación web con diseñador, biblioteca, plantillas, vista previa de archivos y persistencia en `localStorage`.
- El motor local sirve de respaldo; la IA en la nube puede configurarse con Pollinations, una API compatible con OpenAI u Ollama.
- La exportación empaqueta paquetes de comportamiento y recursos, texturas procedurales y un `.mcaddon`.
- La interfaz presenta atributos editables específicos por tipo; las texturas PNG se indican como generadas al exportar.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` carga `ai-engine.js` antes de `app.js`; incluye plantillas de espada y criatura, interfaz de generación y versión visible `1.21.90+`.
- `styles.css` añade estilos para el generador, atributos, vista previa de PNG y ajustes móviles; la comprobación móvil ya no detecta desbordamiento horizontal.
- `app.js` incluye generación, edición de atributos, plantillas con IDs/nombres únicos, exportación ZIP y vista previa del árbol de archivos.
- Se corrigió el rerender de atributos para que los campos no se recreen durante la edición, además de la persistencia de atributos al cambiar de tipo y el evento de blur del ID.
- Pruebas de navegador previas: generación local de objeto, bloque y criatura; generación cloud mediante Pollinations respondió HTTP 200; plantillas y eliminación funcionaron; exportaciones ZIP/JSON y edición manual se probaron.
- Se añadieron ajustes de prioridad de ataque, versión de receta `1.20.10`, componentes de entidades y nomenclatura plural en notificaciones.

### Active
- Volver a ejecutar comprobaciones después de las últimas modificaciones: sintaxis, generación, edición, exportación y validación de referencias/JSON.
- Resolver la diferencia de versiones: `app.js` usa `FORMAT_VERSION = '1.21.90'` y `MIN_ENGINE = [1, 21, 90]`, mientras `ai-engine.js` declara `ENGINE_VERSION = '1.26.60'`.
- Revisar la fidelidad y validez de los componentes Bedrock generados; las pruebas ZIP anteriores no equivalen a importación o jugabilidad en Bedrock.

### Blocked
- No se ha verificado la importación ni la jugabilidad en Minecraft Bedrock.
- No se ha vuelto a probar la exportación tras los cambios más recientes de ZIP, entidades e IA.

## Next Move
1. Ejecutar `node --check app.js` y `node --check ai-engine.js`.
2. Repetir pruebas de navegador para IA local y cloud, atributos manuales de objetos/bloques/criaturas, plantillas, persistencia, filtros y eliminación.
3. Exportar un `.mcaddon` actualizado; comprobar integridad ZIP, JSON, UUID/manifiestos, referencias de texturas/modelos, recetas, loot y spawn rules.
4. Alinear las versiones declaradas y actualizar las afirmaciones de compatibilidad según lo que pueda verificarse.
5. Probar importación y funcionamiento en Bedrock si el entorno lo permite; documentar claramente cualquier validación pendiente.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: generación de contenido, JSON Bedrock, atributos editables, vista previa de archivos y exportación.
- `ai-engine.js`: generación local y saneamiento de respuestas externas; declara la versión del motor.
- `index.html`: interfaz, plantillas, controles y carga de scripts.
- `styles.css`: estilos y ajustes responsivos.
- `README.md`: metadatos actuales del proyecto, aún sin descripción específica de la aplicación.

## Important Context
- Los cambios no están confirmados en Git; el checkpoint previo indicó que los archivos principales aparecen sin seguimiento.
- La prueba cloud de Pollinations generó un objeto, un bloque y una entidad desde la interfaz, pero ocurrió antes de los últimos cambios.
- La exportación anterior pasó la prueba de integridad ZIP y el parseo de JSON; las imágenes PNG verificadas tenían tamaños de 16×16, 64×64 y 128×128.
